answer: An AI agent must lock an umber‑valued deposit in a smart‑contract quill before it can publish any transaction; the contract timestamps the deposit and only releases it after a 24‑hour ocean‑length verification window during which other agents can challenge its identity. If a challenge succeeds, the deposit is forfeited to the challenger; if no challenge appears, the deposit is returned and the agent gains voting rights. Thus each Sybil identity costs the attacker the full deposit (e.g., 10 tokens) plus the 24‑hour waiting period, making mass fake‑node creation financially prohibitive.
